facts.statement: The genus Simolestes was described by Andrews in 1909.
Simolestes lived during the Middle to Late Jurassic periods.
The type specimen of Simolestes vorax is a crushed skeleton found in the Callovian Oxford Clay formation of England.
facts.quote: The type specimen, NHMUK PV R 3319 is an almost complete but crushed skeleton diagnostic to Simolestes vorax, dating back to the Callovian of the Oxford Clay formation, England.

facts.statement: A species named S. indicus from the Tithonian Bhuj Formation of India is tentatively assigned to Simolestes, though this referral is considered dubious.
facts.quote: The genus might also be known from the Tithonian Bhuj Formation of India (S. indicus), but the referral of this species to Simolestes is dubious.

facts.statement: Simolestes had a short, high, and wide skull designed to resist torsional forces during hunting.
facts.quote: Simolestes possessed a short, high, and wide skull which was built to resist torsional forces when hunting.

facts.statement: The largest known specimens of S. vorax reached approximately 4.6 meters in length based on a head-to-body ratio similar to Liopleurodon.
facts.quote: The largest specimens of S. vorax reached approximately 4.6 m in length, if a head to body ratio similar to Liopleurodon is applied.

facts.statement: Simolestes possessed salt-secreting glands that allowed it to maintain salt balance and drink seawater.
facts.quote: Like most pliosaurs, Simolestes possessed salt secreting glands, which would have enabled the animal to maintain salt balance and drink seawater.

facts.statement: Recent studies indicate that Simolestes possessed a unique body plan for movement that differs from modern organisms in similar ecological niches.
facts.quote: Recent studies on plesiosaur locomotion indicate that Simolestes, like other plesiosaurs, possessed a unique bauplan for movement, which differs from modern organisms in similar niches.

facts.statement: The current consensus is that Simolestes was primarily teuthophagous, feeding on belemnites, soft teuthoids, and ammonites.
facts.quote: The current consensus, however, is that the genus was primarily teuthophagous, consuming belemnites, soft teuthoids and ammonites.

facts.statement: Simolestes is classified within the family Rhomaleosauridae.
Simolestes was an extinct genus of rhomaleosaurid pliosauroids that lived in the Middle and Late Jurassic in what is now England and India.
facts.quote: Simolestes es un género extinto de pliosauroides romaleosáuridos que vivieron en el Jurásico medio y el Jurásico superior, en lo que hoy es Inglaterra y la India.

facts.statement: Some sources suggest Simolestes could have exceeded 10 meters in length.
facts.quote: Simolestes podía sobrepasar los 10 metros de longitud.

facts.statement: Simolestes lived from the Bajocian to the Tithonian, approximately 168.6 to 143.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Bajocian to Tithonian (168.6 to 143.1 million years ago)

rejected.statement: It is debated whether Simolestes was ecologically separated from other pliosaurs by hunting in deeper waters or at night, based on the diurnal feeding cycles of modern cephalopods.
rejected.quote: It is possible Simolestes was also ecologically separated from other contemporary pliosaur genera such as Liopleurodon and Pachycostasaurus by hunting in deeper waters or at night, as modern cephalopods exhibit diurnal feeding cycles, spending daylight in deeper, safer waters, and rising at night to feed.
